articles.title: Ubisoft Says Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey Boosted Assassin's Creed Odyssey Sales
articles.summary: Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey sparked a fresh surge in back-catalog sales for 2018's Assassin's Creed Odyssey, Ubisoft has said.
articles.body:
Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey sparked a fresh surge in back-catalog sales for 2018's Assassin's Creed Odyssey , Ubisoft has said.

In its latest financial results briefing, the Assassin's Creed publisher noted how a "major summer movie" had "materially benefited" the continued sales of its brilliant Ancient Greek game. Over the summer, Ubisoft re-promoted Assassin's Creed Odyssey alongside the launch of Nolan's film, inviting players to go start their own epic journey for themselves after returning home from theaters.

Once again, Ubisoft used its financial update to praise the evergreen sales of its Assassin's Creed back catalog. Also, once again, it failed to provide any further detail on how last year's Assassin's Creed Shadows had fared. There's a sense that the long-awaited feudal Japan blockbuster has been a commercial disappointment for Ubisoft, and it's been a while since we had any formal update on sales numbers. No further content for the game is on the way, either — even though 2020's Valhalla just got a New Game Plus mode.

The Odyssey Cast and Characters: Who's Who in the Christopher Nolan Film

Indeed, Shadows is not mentioned at all in the results, despite Ubisoft commenting on Odyssey, Valhalla (which also just passed 40 million players), and this year's Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced — the latter of which has clearly had a successful launch.

Ubisoft attributes an outperformance in its latest financial results to Resynced, which it describes as having been "among the industry's most successful Action-Adventure remakes." How did its launch compare to any all-new Assassin's Creed games? If it did surpass any of those, Ubisoft perhaps understandably isn't saying — but it's clear the game has been a hit.

"The franchise will celebrate its 20th anniversary next year," Ubisoft said, reiterating what fans have heard already — that 2027 should be a more exciting year for the series than the past 12 months have been. "This is a major milestone for the brand, which is preparing a year of reveals, updates, rewards, and community moments."

It seems likely that next year will be when we get a first glimpse of the upcoming Assassin's Creed Hexe, the series' next blockbuster game, as well as Netflix's upcoming Assassin's Creed TV series set in Ancient Rome and a peek at Codename Invictus, a new multiplayer game spinoff. Until then, well, Assassin's Creed: Odyssey is really worth a go if you haven't played it already.

GTA 6 is finally here, and players are already devouring it, finding each and every one of its secrets and surprises at a rapid pace. We have no doubt that some are so well-hidden that we won’t discover them for weeks, months, or even years, but when it comes to others, the cat is firmly out of the bag.

Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? Check out the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN. If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips and Chapter 2 Guide and Tips . If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map .

Why is everyone suddenly talking about Niko Bellic in GTA 6?

Well, yesterday, developer Rockstar finally revealed the GTA 6 credits . Within that long, long webpage is the full cast of actors and the characters they play in the game. One name was snuck in right at the bottom, though. One that would mean a lot to long-term fans of the series: Michael Hollick.

Hollick, for those not well-versed in GTA’s past, voiced the Grand Theft Auto 4 protagonist, Niko Bellic. So, assumptions have been made that the beloved character may well make an appearance in GTA 6. In the credits, the actor is listed as playing someone simply listed as ‘The Hitman.’ The burning question is: Does Niko Bellic have a cameo, or maybe even a larger role in Jason and Lucia’s story, or is this mystery hitman an original character?

Really, do not read past this point if you don’t want any late-game spoilers for GTA 6. While I will not go into what it means for Jason and Lucia’s story, I will be talking about a major surprise you might want to experience yourself. You have been warned.

Yes, ‘The Hitman’ is indeed Niko Bellic. That pseudonym makes a lot of sense — he spends much of his time in GTA 4’s story as a gun for hire, bringing his military experience in the Yugoslav Wars to the streets of Liberty City. And from the looks of him here and the situation we find him in, not a whole lot has changed in the intervening 18 years.

Niko is still heavily involved in the criminal underworld, albeit just dealing with his business with a few extra grey hairs these days, and has been called to Vice City to help eradicate a problem for the people he’s working for. I won’t go into what this means for GTA 6’s tale or how Jason and Lucia find their story connecting to another of the series’ protagonists, but I will confirm that it's all highly enjoyable for the short time we get to meet Mr Bellic again. Sadly, that doesn’t involve going bowling with his cousin.

GTA 4 and Niko are incredibly beloved at this point, with people often citing him as the strongest Grand Theft Auto protagonist to this day. It was a turning point for a more mature era of Rockstar storytelling, ultimately leading to the more empathetic nature of GTA 6’s story. Only time will tell if either Jason or Lucia will be held in such regard as 2008’s Liberty City immigrant with a dream, as more and more people finish their story.

That being said, if you’re someone reading this who has either finished GTA 6, or isn’t fussed about cameo spoilers, please don’t share this with others who you know won’t want to know this information. GTA 6 is a special game, so letting others enjoy it at their own pace with all its secrets and surprises still held up its sleeve is the kindest thing you could do.

We have plenty more GTA 6 coverage for you at IGN, from letting you know how long the game takes to beat to the optional missions you really shouldn’t miss .

articles.title: Paul Thomas Anderson and Benny Safdie's Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall Is an Intimate, Minimalist Experience
articles.summary: Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall review: Paul Thomas Anderson and Benny Safdie bring an intimate concert to the big screen.
articles.body:
Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall is in select theaters on November 20.

Paul Thomas Anderson’s concert movie, Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall, is as stripped-back and threadbare as they come in keeping with its subject: a minimalist solo concert by Geese front man Cameron Winter. The twenty-four-year-old folk artist — twenty-three at the time of filming — sits at a piano on a darkened stage, titled away from the audience, creating a gentle mystery of sorts which Anderson complements with his camera, operated on occasion by producer Benny Safdie. The result will no doubt depend on your interest in Winter’s music, but the documentary evokes a grounded tactility that’s hard to ignore, and whose allure is harder to deny.

With the beeps and boops of mobile ticket scanners, Anderson welcomes us inside the titular concert hall (How do you get there? Practice !) before a hard cut from empty stands to a full and bustling crowd creates anticipation. It’s a far cry from the filmmaker’s other concert movie — the Jodhpur-set Junun — which made use of digital tech like drones to gawk at its Indian musicians like animals in a zoo. Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall feels far more compassionate, as though its director either felt closer to the music or had simply reached greater maturity as a documentarian.

The dim concert space comes alive thanks to the grain of Anderson’s 35mm film — across several cameras — creating an image that feels fluid and rhythmic, even in static moments. It feels no less enveloping even when on-screen audience members occasionally display a lack of etiquette with their cellphones (the movie is, in this way, quite complete and immersive… for better or worse). Between wide shots of Winter hunched over his piano and close-ups of him circling the microphone, surrounded practically by a void, the frame conjures imagery reminiscent of one of the artist’s prominent tracks, “ Try as I May ,” in which he croons: “You were meant to watch my private ceremonies, all in the dark parts of rooms.”

There’s both a religiosity and self-effacing quality to Winter’s poetry, which speaks for itself through the music without Anderson really employing any flourishes beyond the show’s own direction. Lights intermittently come up to illuminate a sparse backdrop reminiscent of an empty home mid-transition, which we’re allowed to glimpse at times. Most of the time, however, the frame is occupied by close-ups of Winter lost in soulful song.

It’s the kind of soothing concert film you could probably zone out or fall asleep to, which is by no means a bad thing in this particular context. Even those unfamiliar with Winter’s music will likely be taken by his dreamlike reflections, peppered with occasional humor through some piano peacocking on the highest keys and a particularly funny interaction with the set itself. But for the most part, the doc and its central performance are as straightforward and classical as they come, even though the music has a modern, alternative vibe.

With slow zooms and push-ins — and on the rarest of occasions, a hand-held follow — Anderson’s approach verges on reverential for the young musical prodigy, which is in keeping with the demands of his late-2025 live show. It’s about the resplendent music more than anything else, including the performance itself, which exists more in the echoes off Carnegie Hall’s historic walls than even the stage from which it emanates, decorated only with intermittent wires. Much like the concert’s designers have chosen to do, Anderson essentially gets out of the way despite having a camera practically affixed to Winter himself — one he keeps entirely invisible until the closing credits, revealing his own illusions only once Winter’s magic has ceased after a mellifluous 72 minutes.

articles.title: Surprise PS5 Console Black Friday Deals Means You Can Buy a GTA 6-Ready Console for Less Than £430
articles.summary: PlayStation has unexpectedly cut PS5 console prices for Black Friday, with refurbished models from £427.49 and up to £30.50 off brand-new consoles
articles.body:
Anyone keen on buying a PS5 to play GTA 6 (you may have heard of it) and other hit games during Black Friday can unexpectedly get up to £30.50 off their new console when buying from PlayStation.

With the new GTA sequel finally out, Amazon and other retailers have already rolled out plenty of early Black Friday discounts, including being able to grab a new PS5 DualSense controller for £42.99 at Amazon , or being able to buy Grand Theft Auto VI for as little as £60.85 over at ShopTo .

However, the biggest surprise of all is over at PlayStation itself; in a huge early Black Friday sale with lots of targeted price cuts of its own, the console manufacturer has inadvertently made it the cheapest store around to grab a PS5 . There is a minor catch, but it’s still the best price you can get following PlayStation’s multiple hardware price increases over the years.

The Cheapest PS5 Console Prices for Black Friday

Certified Refurbished PlayStation 5 Console

Certified Refurbished PlayStation 5 Console (model group - slim)

PlayStation 5 Digital Edition Console - 825 GB

PlayStation 5 Digital Edition Console 825 GB - Two DualSense Wireless Controllers Bundle

PlayStation 5 Console 1 TB - Two DualSense Wireless Controllers Bundle

Specifically, thanks to PlayStation’s bonus 5% off on hardware and accessories for signed-in PlayStation Plus members, the lowest price PS5 you can buy to play GTA 6 on is now £427.49 for the ‘Certified Refurbished’ original PS5 with a disc drive , previously £449.99.

For contrast, that's £22.50 off an already discounted console, and £142.50 less than buying the brand-new 1TB disc-drive PS5 at its usual £569.99 price.

However, depending on what kind of console setup and gaming library you’re going for, there are lots of other discounted PS5s you can grab. For instance, the also- ‘Certified Refurbished’ PS5 Slim console is also cheaper at £455.99 (normally £479.99).

The refurbished PS5 Slim Digital Edition has also been dropped to just £408.49 (normally £429.99), but is currently sold out at the time of writing.

Mind you, these aren't brand-new systems, but Sony does put its Certified Refurbished consoles through a full testing and recertification process, with a 12-month manufacturer's warranty included. Minor cosmetic imperfections are possible, but that's the trade-off for paying considerably less.

For those only interested in booting up Grand Theft Auto 6 on brand-new hardware, the 825GB PS5 Digital Edition is now £493.99 , down from £519.99, whilst the 1TB disc-drive model costs £541.49 , previously £569.99.

Alternatively, if you fancy either having a spare to hot-swap during recharging, or if you want to be set for playing multiplayer games with a friend, you can also get the latter PS5 with two DualSense controllers for £579.49 (was £609.99), saving the full £30.50.

For comparison, that's only £47.50 extra for a disc drive (which can be bought individually for £66.49 ) and another 175GB of storage, compared to buying the standard Digital Edition, making it our pick if you plan to buy physical PS5 games.

PlayStation Plus Memberships Are on Sale, Too, if You Don’t Have One Already

Now, as for the aforementioned catch, these additional 5% discounts on PS5 consoles are only available to those with an active PlayStation Plus membership. That said, you won't necessarily have to spend much extra to take advantage, as some of Sony's subscription plans are also getting some sizable Black Friday price cuts.

To start, you can grab a single month of PS Plus Essential for just £7.99 , which would still leave you with a net saving of up to £22.51 on the most expensive console bundle.

Alternatively, if you were planning on getting a longer membership anyway, the 12-month Essential plan has fallen to £47.99 from its usual £59.99 price — saving you 20%, or effectively bringing your monthly cost down to just £3.99.

Better yet, there's also 25% off annual PS Plus Extra memberships, whilst Premium has received the biggest 33% discount, dropping from £119.99 to £80.39 for a whole year.

PlayStation Plus Essential includes monthly games, online multiplayer, exclusive discounts, cloud storage for game saves, and Share Play.

PlayStation Plus Extra includes everything from Essential, alongside access to hundreds of downloadable PS4 and PS5 games through the Game Catalogue, plus a selection of Ubisoft+ Classics.

PlayStation Plus Premium adds everything from the previous two tiers, along with the Classics Catalogue featuring older PlayStation games, limited-time game trials, and cloud streaming for select PS5 titles.

articles.title: 'Cousin! We Should Hang Out!' GTA Secret Quests Referencing Roman Bellic Added to Fortnite
articles.summary: Fortnite has added a series of secret GTA quests referencing GTA 4's Roman Bellic and the game's memorable "Cousin! We should hang out!" meme.
articles.body:
Fortnite has added a series of secret GTA quests referencing GTA 4's Roman Bellic and his memorable "Cousin! We should hang out!" meme.

Epic Games' battle royale flipped the switch to activate the six secret quests yesterday, the official day of GTA 6's release, allowing players to receive a series of fresh tasks from Peely the banana in exchange for a whopping 120,000 XP.

These quests all reference GTA 4 — and Roman Bellic's frequent harassment of his cousin, protagonist Nico Bellic — by having Fortnite players pick up the phone to Peely, who requests they complete a nearby task. Fittingly, one of Peely's quests involves knocking over a set of bowling pins — a nod to how Roman would call to invite Nico to go bowling with him. "Cousin! We should hang out!" reads the quest's on-screen description.

Other quests direct players to encounter various existing Easter eggs present on Fortnite's current map, including hidden treasure caves, a Zelda-like statue puzzle, and a cute rubber duck race.

Fortnite is currently weathering the launch of GTA 6 fairly well, with player numbers for the game's main evergreen battle royale mode still in the millions despite Rockstar's masterpiece launching this week. Epic Games has done well to build up interest in Fortnite's current season by dangling the oppurtunity to unlock a fortnight of entirely free access to the game's lucrative item shop, something players are now grinding for in huge numbers.

As for GTA 6 itself, Rockstar is yet to reveal exactly how well the game has sold — though it's clear the game has been a huge success, just from the estimated 20 million pre-order copies that the game shifted before launch.
